title: Key Vault vs App Configuration
description: Understand when to use Key Vault versus App Configuration for different types of application settings.

data.text: Key Vault and App Configuration solve overlapping but different problems. Key Vault focuses on protecting secrets and cryptographic material. App Configuration focuses on managing settings and feature flags across environments.

cards.title: Key Vault
cards.description: A secure vault for secrets, keys, and certificates.
cons: Not optimized for dynamic app settings

cards.title: App Configuration
cards.description: A centralized configuration store with feature flags and labels.
cons: Not designed for high-security secrets storage

data.title: Common Pattern
data.text: Use App Configuration for settings and feature flags. Use Key Vault references inside App Configuration for secrets. This keeps your config centralized while keeping secrets secure.

The two services look similar because both store named values, but they defend against different threats. Key Vault assumes the value is dangerous if read: it audits every access, supports hardware-backed keys and certificates, and separates data-plane permissions by object type. App Configuration assumes the value is safe to read by the application but must be changed without redeploying: it offers labels, feature flags, and provider refresh.

data.title: Reference a Key Vault secret from App Configuration
data.content: A Key Vault reference is a normal key whose value is a JSON document with a URI. The App Configuration provider resolves it at load time using the configured credential.

data.title: A practical split
items: Key Vault: database passwords, API keys, storage keys you have not yet retired, TLS certificates, signing keys, encryption keys.
App Configuration: feature flags, endpoint URLs, timeouts, retry counts, batch sizes, tenant mappings, non-secret business settings.
App Configuration referencing Key Vault: when you want one configuration endpoint and centralized refresh.
Neither: values that must be identical across all environments and never change, which can live in code or a shared config file.

rows: Every secret, key, and certificate operation
Versioned secrets and automatic certificate renewal

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Do not answer "use Key Vault for secrets" and stop. Explain the combination: App Configuration for settings and flags, Key Vault references for secrets, one managed identity, and separate role assignments so the app can read settings without being able to read every secret in the vault.

data.title: Split Configuration Correctly
data.description: Refactor an app that stores all settings in appsettings.json to use App Configuration and Key Vault appropriately.
steps: Move 'FeatureXEnabled' to App Configuration as a feature flag.
Move 'ConnectionStrings:Default' to Key Vault and reference it from App Configuration.
Move 'Logging:LogLevel' to App Configuration with a 'production' label.
data.expectedOutcome: App Configuration holds settings and feature flags. Key Vault holds the actual connection string value.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Key Vault for secrets, keys, and certificates.
Use App Configuration for settings and feature flags.
Combine them with Key Vault references for a clean architecture.
